Author: Hirdesh

1 Ma- 3344/2023
 In The High Court Of Madhypradesh
 At G Wa L I O R
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Hirdesh
 On The 8th Of November, 2024
 Misc. Appeal No. 3344 of 2023
 Smt. Shashi And Others
 Versus
 Gaurav Nagvani Vishwakarma And Others
Appearance:
Shri Mahesh Haswani - learned counsel for the appellants.
Shri Dhruv Agarwal, learned counsel for respondent No.3.

ORDER This appeal by Claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the Award dated 25/02/2023 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to the Court of First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia (M.P.) (in short "Claims Tribunal")in Claim Case No. 31/2022 on account of inadequacy of the compensation seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the death of Ajay Singh the 2 MA- 3344/2023 Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,21,200/- along-with 6% per interest per annum in favour of Claimants from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization .

The breakup of compensation amount is as under:

 Future Prospect @ 40% -Rs. 28,800/-

Total Income of deceased -Rs. 1,00,800/-
 Deduction of personal expenses 1/2 -RS. 50,400/-
 Remaining income of deceased -Rs. 50,400/-
 Dependency of deceased  (50,400 X 18 (M) -Rs.9,07,200/-
 Consortium-(44,000X4) -Rs. 1,76,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs. 16,500/-
 Loss of Estate -Rs. 16,500/-
 Transport Expense -Rs. 5000/-
 ----------------------
 TOTAL Rs. 11,21,200/-
4

Learned counsel for the appellants contends that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- per month.
As per the evidence came on record, he was an unskilled labour.

However, accepting earning of deceased as Rs. 8800/- per month, in view of Workman Compensations Act and adding future prospects, applying adequate multiplier, the reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned Award and contended that the 3 MA- 3344/2023 Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.

So far as income of the deceased is concerned, as per the evidence that came on record, he was an unskilled labour, in view of Workman Compensation Act, therefore, his income should be assessed as Rs.8800/- per month.
Therefore, his income is fixed as Rs.88,00/- per month instead of Rs.6,000/- per month as assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is modified as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT Total Income (Rs.8800 pm x 12) Rs- 1,05,600/- PA Future prospects @ 40% Rs.- 42,240/- PA Income and future prospects Rs- 1,47,840/-PA Dependency 1/2 Rs. 73,920/-
Loss of income:- Rs. 13,30,560/-
Other Heads:
 Loss of Consortium-(44,000X2) -Rs. 88,000/-
(Mother, father)
Smt. Shashi vs Gaurav Nagvani Vishwakarma on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165734290/
2

Funeral expenses -Rs. 16,500/-
Loss of Estate -Rs. 16,500/-
 ----------------------
 TOTAL Rs.14,51,560/-
8.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.14,51,560/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.11,21,200/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of 4 MA- 3344/2023 Rs.3,30,360/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
9. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs. 3,30,360/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

10. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
11. In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the claimants stands disposed of.
